newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: VILNIAUS BANK SAYS WILL SEEK NEW RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: VILNIAUS BANK SAYS WILL SEEK NEW RATINGS.

text.p: Lithuania's Vilniaus Bank said on Monday it would seek new credit ratings in the second quarter of 1997.
"In the nearest future, probably in the second quarter, we will decide on the new rating or ratings," Julius Niedvaras, chairman of the bank's board, told a news conference.
He added that the bank would ask Thomson BankWatch to upgrade its current rating and said the bank was mulling the idea of applying for a rating from another agency.

The bank, which said on Monday that its net profit had shot up to 24.4 million litas in 1996 from 2.9 million litas the previous year, acquired a BB- rating from Thomson last fall for its long-term liabilities.
The bank was also awarded a rating of LC-1 for its short-term liabilities in litas, the highest in the BankWatch scale.
The bank, which is 90 percent foreign owned, is Lithuania's largest private bank.
It doubled its share of the Lithuanian market last year, reaping the benefits of a crisis which shook public confidence in many of the country's other banks.
It is one of the leading blue chip companies on the country's bourse.
